title: Classical Weil local operators and finite-fibre comparison data
statement: Fix a finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a separated finite-type scheme over its finite field, a prime ell different from its characteristic and an algebraic closure Omega of Q_ell. A classical lisse Weil object is the pair in the classical adic category [def-wf-fundamental-representation; def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] with its specified automorphism pullback [def-wf-lisse-adic-automorphism-pullback]. Define its one-step fibre map by the inverse canonical pullback-fibre isomorphism followed by the fibre of its Weil map; iterate using the literal orbit of geometric Frobenius. For a finite-etale fibre-functor path, define the local operator by the induced adic basepoint transport [def-pod-lisse-adic-fibre-functors] followed by these steps. For a finite sf Weil model [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], take degree-zero cohomology of the normalized local point complex [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], lift its module carrier and extend coefficients through the canonical inclusion into Omega. The fibre comparison datum is an isomorphism between this extended finite fibre and the classical fibre at every geometric point; for every positive return iterate it intertwines the local Frobenius map with the classical operator for a finite-etale path acting on every cover by precomposition with that same point Frobenius iterate. The induced map between finite fibres is the same pullback, cohomology, carrier-lift and coefficient-extension composite applied to a Weil morphism.
